# tfutils_aws_eni_released_wait_and_delete (Resource)

Creates nothing. Unlike `tfutils_aws_eni_released_wait`, this resource deletes ENIs. On destroy, waits until the VPC has no amazon-vpc-cni ENI of the cluster that is `available` or whose attachment is `detaching`, and no ENI of a node that is `shutting-down`. While the node of an ENI runs, vpc-cni deletes the ENI and this resource only waits. An `available` ENI whose node is terminated or no longer exists has no owner left, so this resource deletes it and reports the deleted ENIs as a warning. Destroy fails with the remaining ENIs when the delete timeout passes. Make the resources whose deletion terminates the nodes depend on this resource, so that destroy runs it after the nodes are terminated.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "tfutils_aws_eni_released_wait_and_delete" "vpc_cni" {
  vpc_id       = var.vpc_id
  cluster_name = var.cluster_name

  timeouts {
    delete = "10m"
  }
}

resource "kubectl_manifest" "nodepool" {
  yaml_body = var.nodepool_yaml

  depends_on = [tfutils_aws_eni_released_wait_and_delete.vpc_cni]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_name` (String) Value of the `cluster.k8s.amazonaws.com/name` tag that vpc-cni puts on the cluster's ENIs.
- `vpc_id` (String) VPC of the cluster.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<vpc_id>/<cluster_name>`.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
